findings.title: Custom FallbackLocaleList replaces full-featured I18n::Locale::Fallbacks with a minimal stand-in
findings.body: Previously `config.i18n.fallbacks = true` assigned a standard `I18n::Locale::Fallbacks` instance, which implements the full fallback API (`map`, `default`, `defaults`, locale-tag decomposition such as `pt-BR -> pt -> en`, etc.). The new `FallbackLocaleList` only overrides `[]` and `ensure_loaded!`; all other Hash/Fallbacks methods are either absent or behave as an empty Hash. Any code (core, plugin, or gem) that calls other methods on `I18n.fallbacks` besides `[]` will now silently misbehave or raise NoMethodError, and locale-tag-based fallback behavior (e.g. regional variants) is lost without an equivalent compatibility shim.

findings.title: Required initializer ordering is enforced only by a comment, not by code
findings.body: The file relies on `02-freedom_patches.rb` having already patched `I18n::Backend::Simple`/`I18n::Backend::Base` (translate_accelerator) before this initializer runs, but the only indication of that dependency is the comment `# order: after 02-freedom_patches.rb`. Rails initializer load order is driven by filename sort order; there is no explicit `require` or `config.before_initialize`/`after_initialize` hook enforcing the sequence. If the freedom-patch filename or load mechanism changes, this file could load before the patches are applied, causing `I18n::Backend::Simple` to not have the LRU-cache/explicit-load behavior when `I18n::Backend::Fallbacks` is mixed in, or vice versa, leading to subtle load-order bugs.

findings.title: Fallback behavior is now enabled globally instead of per-environment, silently changing dev/test behavior
findings.body: `config.i18n.fallbacks = true` was previously set only in production.rb, profile.rb and the cloud66 production.rb — i.e. selectively per environment. By moving the equivalent logic into `config/initializers/i18n.rb` (which loads for all environments including development and test), locale fallbacks are now always active everywhere. This is a behavior change that isn't called out in the PR description, and it means missing-translation issues that previously surfaced in development/test (because fallback wasn't enabled there) will now be silently masked by falling back to the default locale/English, potentially hiding real translation bugs until they reach users of other locales in production.

findings.title: ensure_loaded! recomputes fallback chain (including a SiteSetting lookup) on every request
findings.body: `I18n.fallbacks.ensure_loaded!` is invoked unconditionally in `set_locale`, a before_filter run on every request. Internally this calls `FallbackLocaleList#[]`, which reads `SiteSetting.default_locale` on every single request just to build the (mostly already-loaded) fallback chain. While the actual file loading is memoized via `@loaded_locales`, the SiteSetting lookup and array construction happen on every request regardless, adding avoidable per-request overhead that the translate_accelerator patch was specifically designed to minimize.

findings.title: No tests added for the new fallback resolution logic
findings.body: The PR introduces new runtime logic (`FallbackLocaleList#[]`, `FallbackLocaleList#ensure_loaded!`, `I18n.ensure_loaded!` in translate_accelerator.rb, and the new call in `ApplicationController#set_locale`) but adds no specs verifying that: (1) translations correctly fall back from user locale -> site default locale -> English, (2) `ensure_loaded!` actually loads the right locale files, or (3) `set_locale` behaves correctly when a translation is missing in the user's locale. Given this is a user-facing localization feature, lacking any automated coverage is a significant gap.

findings.title: PR description is a non-descriptive placeholder
findings.body: The PR description is simply "Test 9", which provides no information about the rationale, scope, or testing performed for this localization fallback feature. This makes it difficult for reviewers or future maintainers to understand why the change was made or what edge cases were considered.
